feed.title: NPR Topics: World
feed.subtitle: NPR world news, international art and culture, world business and financial markets, world economy, and global trends in health, science and technology. Subscribe to the World Story of the Day podcast and RSS feed.

entry.title: The UN passed resolution ahead of General Assembly calling for end to child marriage
entry.summary: The UN estimates 650 million women and girls currently alive were married before age 18. A new resolution aims to bring awareness and push countries to act to end child marriage.

entry.title: As Nepal identifies those killed in the floods, questions grow over China's reporting
entry.summary: One week after the deadly floods, very little is known about China's dead or missing. China's control over media and digital censorship is in stark contrast to open reporting in Nepal.

entry.title: 5 dead after crash at Miami Airport. And, Germany's far-right wins state election
entry.summary: A cargo plane crash at Miami International Airport has left five people dead and several others injured. And, Germany's far-right AfD party achieves an electoral victory in a key state election.

entry.title: Kushner and Witkoff visit Ukraine with hopes of restarting peace talks with Russia
entry.summary: For the first time, Trump's top envoys take their peace push to Kyiv — after talks with Putin in Moscow.

entry.title: Former U.S. ambassador to Ukraine on efforts to strike a compromise with Russia
entry.summary: NPR's Leila Fadel asks William Taylor, former U.S. ambassador to Ukraine, about efforts made by U.S. emissaries toward a compromise between Russia and Ukraine.

entry.title: Rubio to visit 3 Latin American countries this week
entry.summary: Secretary of State Marco Rubio heads to Colombia, Peru and Ecuador as President Trump hails a shift to the right in regional politics and a new era of U.S. dominance.

entry.title: U.S. envoys visit Kyiv for first time after meeting Putin in Moscow
entry.summary: US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff made their first trip to Kyiv, one day after meeting Vladimir Putin in Moscow.

entry.title: Shipping companies are putting sails back on cargo ships
entry.summary: One of the world's largest logistics companies plans to fit one of its ships with a strange type of sail, the latest in a small but growing number of cleaner sailing shipping vessels.

entry.title: What Russia and China learned from America after 9/11
entry.summary: Journalists Mikhail Zygar and Cindy Yu explain how the wars in Iraq and Afghanistan helped reshape Russia and China's ambitions.

entry.title: Germany's far-right achieves an electoral breakthrough in key state election
entry.summary: Germany's populist, far-right Alternative for Germany party has declared victory in the state of Saxony-Anhalt after more than doubling its share of the vote in the first of several regional elections this fall.
